content.text:
**Verdict: the evidence supports a network fault on the ts-user→ts-auth link, consistent with `network_loss` (or `network_partition`, which the equivalence class scores the same). I'd put confidence at moderate, not high.** The claim is only partly supported as stated, because the lead's third data point is about a different fault.

**What supports a network fault on the ts-user→auth link**
- The lead's gap numbers reproduce. Of the 15 matched ts-user→auth POST calls in the abnormal period, most have a normal gap (~1.2 ms), but three have large gaps: ~207 ms, ~631 ms and ~645 ms. Time is lost between the two ends of the call, not inside either process.
- The slowness is confined to that one pair. ts-user's own MySQL traffic (`SELECT`, `INSERT`, `DELETE ts.user`) is unchanged (p95 ~0.2–0.3 ms, same as normal). admin-user→ts-user POST and PUT gaps are flat (~1.2 ms and ~0.2 ms), so the wire to ts-user is fine elsewhere.
- The median gap is unchanged, which rules out `network_delay`. Delay would add a similar amount to every call on the connection, and most calls here are normal.
- The long tail with values near 200, 400 and 600+ ms fits TCP retransmission backoff, which is the loss signature.
- Clock skew is unlikely: a skew would shift gaps by a constant, not produce sporadic 600 ms outliers.
- ts-user's pod shows no restarts. Uptime rises monotonically from 598 s to 868 s and `k8s.pod.network.errors` is 0 throughout. So this is not `pod_failure` or `pod_unavailable` on ts-user.
- One ts-user POST (the 26.6 s client span on the registerUser path) has no child server span at all. That fits a request that never got through, which is compatible with loss or partition, but it is one sample.

**What weakens the claim as stated**
- The lead's third point is about ts-auth, not the link. `AuthController.createDefaultUser` (p95 ~74 ms normal → ~280 ms abnormal, n=46) and the auth `POST /api/v1/auth` server span (p95 ~281 ms) do rise. But one of the slow calls has server time of 281 ms and a client-minus-server gap of only 1.2 ms. That slowdown happens inside auth, so it is an `application_method_slow`-type signal on auth, not evidence for network loss. It doesn't contradict the link finding, but it means the "auth server stays at ~75 ms" framing in the lead's evidence is wrong for some calls.
- The sample is small: roughly 15 matched calls, of which about 3–4 are wire outliers. Many ts-user POST client spans also have no child span even when normal (~76 ms), so missing child spans are common in this dataset and don't by themselves indicate a fault.
- Log checks did not run successfully (the first attempt used a wrong column name and the second returned empty rows), so I have no log-level evidence either way. No per-connection `hubble_*` metrics exist for this case, so I can't see packet-level loss directly.

**Alternatives considered**
- `network_delay`: ruled out by the flat median gap and the sporadic tail.
- `http_slow` / `http_aborted`: the extra time sits between the client and server spans, not inside the HTTP handling. All responses are 201 with no error status.
- `application_method_slow` on ts-user: the ts-user server and internal spans are normal; the time sits on the client span.
- `dns_lookup_failed`: no name-resolution text found in traces; logs unchecked.
- `network_loss` vs `network_partition`: the data can't separate them, and they are equivalent for scoring.
